name: Claude Certified Architect – Foundations
audience: Engineers who design and ship Claude-based systems: agents, tools, Claude Code setups and extraction pipelines
format: 60 scenario-based multiple-choice items in 120 minutes; scaled score 100–1000, pass 720. Four scenarios drawn from a bank of six.
verifyNotes: Exam facts come from third-party summaries of Anthropic's v1.0 guide (July 2026); the official guide is in Anthropic Partner Academy and not public. Verify Claude product facts (API, Claude Code, MCP, Agent SDK) against docs.claude.com, modelcontextprotocol.io and anthropic.com/engineering.
scenarios: Customer support agent with tools and escalation
Developer productivity tooling for a team

domains.name: Agentic Architecture & Orchestration
skills: Control an agent loop with stop_reason (end_turn, tool_use, max_tokens, pause_turn, refusal); iteration and budget caps as safety nets only
Choose workflow vs agent and pick among prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers and evaluator-optimizer
Design orchestrator/sub-agent systems with clear objectives, output formats, tool allowlists and context isolation
Decompose tasks statically or dynamically
Design escalation and human-in-the-loop triggers and structured handoffs
Place enforcement on the spectrum from prompt guidance to schemas, hooks, permissions and code
Use Claude Agent SDK concepts: hooks, permissions, subagents, sessions, max turns and budgets
Handle failures: transient retries, alternate strategies, stopping and reporting instead of looping

domains.name: Claude Code Configuration & Workflows
skills: Place instructions in the CLAUDE.md hierarchy (managed, user, project, local) and use @imports
Use path-scoped rules in .claude/rules
Configure settings.json scopes and allow/ask/deny permissions; managed settings for org policy
Choose between hooks, subagents, skills and slash commands
Use plan mode for risky or unfamiliar changes
Run Claude Code headless in CI with -p, JSON output, restricted tools and turn limits; GitHub Actions
Share team configuration: committed settings, .mcp.json, shared skills and agents

domains.name: Prompt Engineering & Structured Output
skills: Write clear, direct prompts with context and motivation
Structure prompts with XML tags and use diverse few-shot examples
Elicit reasoning with chain-of-thought or extended thinking
Prefer principles over long conditional rule lists; avoid instruction dilution
Produce structured output with structured outputs or forced tool use; validate and retry with errors
Split stable system-prompt content from per-request user content
Version prompts and run regression evals on changes

domains.name: Tool Design & MCP Integration
skills: Write tool descriptions and input schemas that steer correct tool choice
Keep toolsets small, distinct and well named; consolidate overlapping tools
Use tool_choice (auto, any, tool, none) and handle parallel tool calls
Return structured errors with is_error; distinguish transient, permanent and uncertain-state failures; idempotency
Explain MCP architecture: hosts, clients, servers; tools, resources, prompts; sampling, roots, elicitation
Choose transports (stdio, Streamable HTTP) and scopes (local, project .mcp.json, user)
Apply MCP trust and least privilege; treat tool results as untrusted data (prompt injection)

domains.name: Context Management & Reliability
skills: Budget the context window; lost-in-the-middle and recency effects
Use prompt caching with stable prefixes first and variable content last
Compact long sessions and keep structured notes or memory files
Isolate context with sub-agents and just-in-time retrieval
Order long documents first and the question last; quote extraction; provenance and citations
Retry 429/529 with backoff and jitter; timeouts; fallbacks; Batch API for offline work
Use independent reviewer instances instead of self-review
